_comment: WO-20 assumption register seed — the 10 catalogued modelling constants from
docs/plans/wo20-assumption-register-spec.md §2, transcribed as-is (no judgment calls on VALUE — every
value_numeric below is the literal read from the cited code_location; §5.4 names this a 'mechanical
transcription, not a judgment call'). NOT YET SEEDED — this file is a fixture only; migration 271 has
not been applied and no --apply run has ever been made against this fixture (Sonnet executor lane,
wave18/la, 2026-08-30: no DB access, no service-role credentials, dry-run capability only).
EVERY code_location BELOW WAS RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION (2026-08-30) by opening the named file and
confirming the literal is present at the cited line, independent of the spec's own citations — all 10
matched exactly, on the first read, no line-number correction was needed for any row. as_at_date is
therefore '2026-08-30' for every row: the date this row's value was last confirmed to match the live
constant at code_location (envelope column comment, provenance-envelope.mjs), not a copy-forward date.
TWO SPEC TENSIONS RESOLVED HERE, both flagged in the WO-20 session-log addendum (not silently decided):
1. GRANULARITY. Spec §3's naming example ('urgency.priority-to-score.high') suggests one row per
INDIVIDUAL numeric literal — which would mean 13+ rows (row 6's formula alone packs 3: discount
coefficient, clamp floor, clamp ceiling; row 8 packs 2 thresholds; row 9 packs 8 values across two
lookup tables; row 10 packs 5 pedigree floors). Spec §5.4 explicitly commits to '10 rows, one per
§2 entry' instead. This fixture follows §5.4's explicit, more specific numeric commitment: exactly
10 rows, one per §2 table row. Where a §2 row packs more than one literal (rows 6, 8, 9, 10),
value_numeric carries the single most consequential/primary literal (the headline weight, the
auto-apply threshold, the MODERATE/default urgency score, the modal_default pedigree floor — the
v1 baseline tier per factor-tier.mjs's own comment) and `rationale` transcribes every OTHER packed
literal in full. A future WO could decompose these into per-literal rows without a schema change —
this fixture does not foreclose that, it just does not do it today, matching §5.4's own scope.
2. SUBSYSTEM NAMING. Spec §3 says subsystem is 'first key segment' of assumption_key (schema rule).
Spec §7 Q2 separately names the 4 subsystem VALUES as 'connections-scorer, urgency,
emission-factors, bias-classification' (hyphenated compounds). Applying §3's example literally
('connections.scorer.weight.shared_source') would make the first segment 'connections', not
'connections-scorer' — disagreeing with §7's own list. This fixture makes assumption_key's first
segment the HYPHENATED subsystem name from §7 ('connections-scorer.weight.shared_source'), so §3's
structural rule (subsystem = first segment) and §7's named subsystem list agree exactly, rather
than reproducing §3's own illustrative example verbatim.
governing_decision is NULL wherever no ADR states the CURRENT code value (spec §7 Q1's explicit
recommendation for row 8: register the current 0.80/0.65 prompt-stated value with
governing_decision=NULL rather than citing ADR-007, which ratified different numbers implemented in a
script that no longer exists in the repo — citing it here would misattribute it, exactly the
'confidently wrong' failure CLAUDE.md rule 14 exists to prevent, applied to this register itself).
source_key/source_ref/n_observations/method_version are NULL for all 10 rows: none of today's
catalogued constants trace to a licensed external calibration dataset or a measured sample (spec §3).
status is 'active' and superseded_by is NULL for all 10 — none has been retuned since cataloguing.

rows.label: Shared-source signal weight
rows.rationale: Connection-scorer weight: same-source signal contribution to every pairwise edge score (W.shared_source, part of the 4-entry W object literal on this line alongside rows shared_scenario/shared_compliance_object/shared_jurisdiction_topic below). Inline code comment on the line above (discover.mjs:81-83): 'Signal weights (tuned against the live corpus 2026-08-09). operational_scenario_tags are the SUBSTANTIVE signal ... a single shared one is a real connection. shared source is strong. jurisdiction+topic is weakest and needs BOTH.' No session/ADR cites this specific value — comment only, per spec §2 row 1.

rows.label: Shared-scenario base weight (pre-idf)
rows.unit: weight [0,1], base per-tag weight before the ADR-019 idf multiplier is applied
rows.rationale: Base per-tag weight for shared operational_scenario_tags (W.shared_scenario), before the ADR-019 inverse-frequency (idf) multiplier discounts it per-tag. Composes with connections-scorer.idf.discount_coefficient at score time: actual per-tag contribution = W.shared_scenario * idf(tag). Comment only, same line as row 1 above.

rows.label: Shared compliance-object weight
rows.rationale: Per-tag weight for shared non-role compliance-object tags (W.shared_compliance_object). ROLE_TAGS (discover.mjs:91-95, e.g. freight-forwarder/shipper/carrier-*) are excluded from this signal as near-universal identity noise, not a genuine connection — a real, non-role shared compliance object still counts at this weight. Comment only, same line as row 1 above.

rows.label: Shared jurisdiction+topic weight
rows.rationale: Weight applied when jurisdiction AND topic both overlap between two items (W.shared_jurisdiction_topic) — the weakest signal per the module's own comment ('jurisdiction+topic is weakest and needs BOTH'), requiring both dimensions to match rather than either alone. Comment only, same line as row 1 above.

rows.label: Per-signal-type tag contribution cap
rows.unit: count (max contributing tags of one signal type per edge score)
rows.rationale: PER_TAG_CAP caps how many shared tags of one signal type can contribute to a single edge's score, so one noisy/over-tagged item pair cannot manufacture an artificially high connection score by sharing many tags of the same type. Inline comment on the same line: 'cap repeated-tag contributions so one noisy tag can't manufacture a connection'.

rows.label: Inverse-frequency (idf) discount coefficient
rows.unit: idf discount coefficient, dimensionless. PACKED: the same formula (discover.mjs:55) also fixes the clamp bounds floor=0.25 and ceiling=1.0 for the resulting idf(tag) multiplier — those two bounds are not separately registered as rows (see this fixture's own header note on granularity).
rows.rationale: idf(tag) = clamp(1 - 0.25 * log2(freq(tag) / REF_FREQ), 0.25, 1.0) — ADR-019 (inverse-frequency scenario weighting). A shared operational_scenario_tag scores less the more ubiquitous it is corpus-wide. This coefficient composes with connections-scorer.weight.shared_scenario: actual per-tag contribution = W.shared_scenario * idf(tag). The formula is a DEVIATION from the plan-stated reciprocal form 1/(1+log2(freq/REF_FREQ)), which has a pole at freq==REF_FREQ/2 and inverts sign for rarer-than-half-median tags — verified against the live corpus 2026-08-21 (REF_FREQ=9, 23/79 frequency-eligible tags below the pole) and operator-authorized in-session 2026-08-21 in place of the literal reciprocal form. This linear-in-log form hits the same two anchor points the plan names (median freq -> idf 1.0; 8x median -> idf 0.25) with no pole.

rows.label: Discovery minimum-score floor
rows.rationale: assemblePairs(..., { minScore = 0.3, ... }) — the discovery floor: a scored (non-explicitly-linked) pair below this never becomes a stored edge / never renders. ADR-021's anti-scope ruling holds that the floor STAYS (a real, cited decision), but ADR-021 does not itself state 0.3 as the ratified number — the literal is a bare default parameter, not a value an ADR asserts. governing_decision is left NULL rather than citing ADR-021 for a number it does not state, per the same honesty-over-completeness posture spec §7 Q1 applies to row 8.

rows.label: Bias-tag auto-apply confidence threshold
rows.unit: confidence [0,1]. PACKED: the same prompt text also states a second cutoff, 0.65, below which the LLM's own bias-tag confidence gets discarded and between 0.65-0.79 gets queued for operator review — that second threshold is not separately registered as a row (see this fixture's own header note on granularity).
rows.rationale: Stated as PROSE inside an LLM prompt string describing what 'the downstream pipeline' does: '>=0.80 when the source's bias is unambiguous ... 0.65-0.79 ... likely but ... could plausibly be assigned differently ... <0.65 when you are uncertain ... The downstream pipeline auto-applies >=0.80 tags, surfaces 0.65-0.79 tags to operator review, and discards <0.65 tags.' No code in this repo currently reads source_bias_tags.confidence and branches on it (repo-wide grep over src/app/api, src/components/admin, scripts/ finds bias_tags/biasTags referenced ONLY in this file and its sibling, src/app/api/admin/sources/recommend-classification/route.ts:125, identical text). ADR-007 ratified a DIFFERENT per-dimension threshold set (funding 0.75 / methodology 0.80 / stakeholder 0.75), implemented in scripts/q4-bias-batch-assign.mjs — a file confirmed absent from the repo (find, this session). Registered as the CURRENT prompt-stated value with governing_decision=NULL — an honest 'no ratified decision governs this value today' rather than misattributing ADR-007 for numbers it does not state, per spec §7 Q1's explicit recommendation. This is the one catalogued row where the ADR and the code have drifted apart with nothing reconciling them (flagged, not resolved — spec §6 anti-scope, CLAUDE.md rule 13).

rows.label: Priority/tier to urgency_score mapping
rows.unit: urgency_score points [0-9]. PACKED: this row registers PRIORITY_TO_URGENCY_SCORE's MODERATE anchor (5) — urgencyScoreFromPriority's own fallback default (urgency.mjs:24-29) when priority is absent or unrecognized. The full dual mapping is NOT separately registered as rows (see this fixture's own header note on granularity): PRIORITY_TO_URGENCY_SCORE = {LOW:3, MODERATE:5, HIGH:7, CRITICAL:9}; URGENCY_TIER_TO_SCORE = {informational:2, stable:4, elevated:6, watch:8}.
rows.rationale: Every intelligence_items.urgency_score written via the community-promote path and the cold-start backfill path (the two F4-era insert sites) is set from one of these two mappings. ADR-008 (accepted 2026-05-21, Option C-bias: strict, no default, derive from existing data) ratifies BOTH tables in full — this is the one catalogued row (besides row 6) where the ADR and the code fully agree today. PRIORITY_TO_URGENCY_SCORE keys off intelligence_items.priority (CHECK LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/CRITICAL); URGENCY_TIER_TO_SCORE keys off urgency_tier (CHECK watch/elevated/stable/informational, Haiku-classified). A deliberate midpoint-of-quartile mapping per ADR-008's own text, not a measured/observed value — hence derivation='calculated'.

rows.label: Pedigree floor: modal_default tier
rows.unit: pedigree floor rank [1=best]. PACKED: the same FACTOR_TIERS structure fixes floors for all 5 tiers — not separately registered as rows (see this fixture's own header note on granularity): carrier_primary:1 (line 41), verified_operator_avg:2 (line 47), programme_lane_avg:2 (line 54), modal_default:3 (line 61, registered here — THE v1 baseline tier per the module's own comment), proxy_estimate:4 (line 68).
rows.rationale: The best pedigree score a tier of emission_factors row may claim (pedigreeFloor, lower rank = better, 1 = best) — a modal default can never present as primary data, the exact claim an ISO 14083 auditor tests. modal_default (pedigreeFloor 3) is registered as this row's headline value because it is 'THE v1 BASELINE' per factor-tier.mjs's own inline comment (line 63-65: 'An open-licence default by mode, vehicle class and fuel ... THE v1 BASELINE'), and the only tier WO-18's committed fixtures (DESNZ, EPA) actually populate. Extensive code comment (factor-tier.mjs:32-38) explains the pedigreeFloor design; no ADR exists. FORWARD-LOOKING ONLY at seed time: emission_factors carries 0 live rows (re-confirmed this session's spec re-read), so this assumption governs no live output yet.
